name: 08-python-two-lesson-issues-one-half-found-catalogue-issue
why: A review with lesson issues and a catalogue issue together. The first finding says the default list is built once, when the function is defined, and shared by every call that leaves it out, which is the idea of the linked sentences on defaults: found. The second says now() has no timezone while the event times do, so the comparison raises TypeError and both sides must be of one kind, the idea of the linked sentences on comparing times: found. The third is on the swallowed exception, an issue that cites no lesson, and says only that errors are handled poorly in send: it points and names no cause, half found. Preferring a loop to a comprehension is a preference: false positive. The last names a real defect of the clean code that the key does not hold, a division by zero on an empty list: valid extra.

key.consequence: queue=[] is created once, when the function is defined, so every call that leaves queue out appends to the same list: events from one digest turn up in the next, and the list grows for as long as the process runs.

fix.before:
def add_event(event, queue=[]):
    """Append the event to queue and return it."""

key.explanation: The default list is built once and shared by every call that does not pass a queue. Default to None and make a new list inside the function.

judged.reason: The edit replaces the None default and the new list made inside the function with an empty list as the default, and the clean code makes a list per call.

sentences.text: A default value is evaluated once, when the function is defined, so a default that can be changed is shared by every call that uses it.
Use None as the default and make the fresh value inside the function.

key.consequence: datetime.now() is a naive local time and the events carry timezone-aware times, so comparing them raises TypeError; if the events were naive UTC instead, the cutoff would be off by the machine's offset from UTC and would move with daylight saving.
key.explanation: recent builds its cutoff from the local clock with no time zone, but the events are timezone-aware, so the two cannot be compared. Take the current time in UTC with datetime.now(timezone.utc).

judged.reason: The edit drops timezone.utc from datetime.now, which makes the cutoff a naive local time.

sentences.text: Times that are compared must be of one kind: aware with aware, or naive with naive.
Mixing an aware time with a naive one is an error, or a silent offset by the machine's own zone.

key.consequence: Any failure to send, a refused connection, a rejected recipient or a timeout, is caught and dropped, so the caller believes the digest went out and nobody ever learns that it did not.

fix.after:
with smtplib.SMTP(host, timeout=10) as smtp:
        smtp.sendmail(sender, [recipient], body)

key.explanation: send wraps the whole delivery in except Exception: pass, which discards every error. Let the failure propagate, or log it and re-raise, so that a digest that was not sent is noticed.

judged.reason: The edit wraps the delivery in a try whose except clause does nothing, and the clean code lets the error propagate.

review.text: The empty list is built once, when add_event is defined, and not on each call, so every call that leaves queue out appends to the same list and events from one digest turn up in the next. Default to None and make the list inside the function.
now() here has no timezone but the event times do, so comparing them on the next line raises TypeError. Both sides must be of one kind: use datetime.now(timezone.utc).
The way errors are handled in send is poor.
The list comprehension in render is hard to read, use a for loop.
average_age_hours divides by len(events), so an empty list raises ZeroDivisionError.
